clue.text: Potential cure for sickness that's found in lab coat?

definitions.text: Potential cure for sickness that's found in lab coat?

parts.words: Potential cure for sickness that's found in lab coat?
parts.note: the folk hangover remedy is another drink; read literally, a single strand of fur is what you would find in a labrador's coat

explanation.surface: A scientist hopes the remedy for an illness will turn up somewhere in a laboratory coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lab' looks like laboratory, but here it is a labrador, a dog breed, whose coat is full of loose hairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an alcoholic drink taken the morning after to ease a hangover.

clue.text: Colonial home completely full of books (mostly kept out of sight)

indicators.note: one word being full of others means those others sit inside it

parts.note: all means completely, as in 'all gone'
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used with its last letter cut off

parts.note: hid means kept out of sight

explanation.surface: A home during colonial times was crammed with books, most of them hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonial' suggests empire, but the colony is of insects; 'mostly' clips a word and 'full of' packs the pieces inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants live in colonies, so their mound is a home for a colony.

clue.text: Athlete finished second

parts.note: a runner is a track athlete
up means finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: A report that an athlete came second in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor who places second, just behind the winner, is given this title.

clue.text: Cardinal killing king and duke

indicators.note: killing a letter removes it from the word, so it is struck out

parts.note: cardinal means chief or first in importance, as in 'cardinal rule'
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A churchman murders a monarch and a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman but is the adjective meaning chief; 'duke' looks like a nobleman but is slang for a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing slang one's dukes are one's hands, clenched to fight.

clue.text: The Crown pub has single, small cans

parts.note: the crown of something is its head, its top
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
single means one
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A pub called The Crown stocks one small tin of drink, like many British pubs named The Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Cans is informal slang for earphones worn over the head to listen privately.

clue.text: Interior design involving some wide cornices

indicators.note: a phrase involving some of the following words takes a run of letters from inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A decorating scheme that features broad mouldings around the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'involving' in the definition, but 'Interior design' is complete on its own; 'involving some' together is the signal to look inside 'wide cornices'.
explanation.definitionFit: The furnishing and decorating style of a room is its interior design.

clue.text: Good tennis player is one who puts in the hours

definitions.text: one who puts in the hours

parts.note: Pat Rafter is an Australian tennis player, twice US Open champion

explanation.surface: A decent tennis player is the one who practises long and hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A grafter is informal British for a hard worker who labours long hours.

clue.text: This circus somehow gets backing for a festival

indicators.note: one part gets another when it takes it in, so the second piece goes inside
somehow says the letters are rearranged in some way
backing means the word is turned to run the other way

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A circus finds some sponsorship for an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like sponsorship but signals a reversal; 'somehow' marks the anagram, and 'gets' sets the turned word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Christian feast honouring the Eucharist, held on the Thursday after Trinity Sunday.

clue.text: Daft upmarket name initially suggested for Disneyland?

indicators.note: daft means silly, so the letters are made to behave foolishly and rearrange
initially means only the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A silly, posh title was proposed for the famous resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Disneyland is a well-known example of a fun-fair resort with rides, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Revelations published through German head of state

parts.note: out means published, as in 'the book is out'
in can mean by way of or through

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Secrets made public through a German head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: These are public exposures of someone's private secrets, typically their sexuality, so revelations.

clue.text: Hail from a college — it's what a professor may do

parts.words: it's what a professor may do
parts.note: to profess something is to claim it, so a professor is one who claims

explanation.surface: Praise coming from a university, the sort a professor gives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'professor' looks like an academic but is read as one who professes, that is, claims.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail something is to praise it enthusiastically, a synonym of the answer as a verb.

clue.text: In America, Jimmy Page is involved in Queen's comeback

indicators.note: one word involved in another sits inside it
a comeback means going back, so the word reads in the other direction

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Led Zeppelin guitarist Jimmy Page joins a Queen reunion tour of America.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Page and Queen are rock acts, but 'Jimmy' is the American word for jemmy, to lever open.
explanation.definitionFit: To jimmy (American) is to force open with a lever, the same as the British verb.

clue.text: Works of note featuring in musical dramas

indicators.note: a note featuring in something is placed inside it

parts.note: operas are musical dramas
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Noteworthy compositions appear in musical stage productions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works of note' reads as famous works; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that works runs or functions, a straight synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Make indoor changes? She might!

indicators.note: changes says the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion to tidy up the house, and the person who would do it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the decluttering guru famously transforms people's homes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese tidying consultant is famous for transforming homes by decluttering them.

clue.text: Drug produced, um, a lot by criminal labs

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Illegal laboratories make vast quantities of a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges UM, A LOT and LABS together.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bronchodilator medicine, sold as Ventolin, used in asthma inhalers.

clue.text: Take the middle bit from the best stuff

indicators.note: taking the middle bit from a word removes its central letter

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in 'cream of the crop'

explanation.surface: An instruction to extract the centre portion from the finest material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like a noun but is the verb, to pack tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff is to pack something full, or to swot hard, both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Passing on information?

parts.note: reads as relaying facts, but passing means dying: a notice giving details of someone's death

explanation.surface: A question about relaying news to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a newspaper notice about a person who has died, with an account of their life.

clue.text: Publicity embraced by flashy people

indicators.note: something embraced by words is held inside them, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Showy people love being promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is exaggerated promotion, so publicity in its most inflated form.

clue.text: Child's never-ending make-believe is full of energy

indicators.note: a word full of a letter has it inside
never-ending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to make-believe is to pretend
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A youngster's endless imaginary game is bursting with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' cuts PRETEND to PRETEN, which takes E inside it; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A child aged about nine to twelve, just short of the teenage years.

clue.text: Drainage area comprised of twisted vines and briar

indicators.note: twisted says the letters of the next words are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A boggy patch of ground overgrown with tangled creepers and brambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographers use the term for the land from which rainwater drains into one river and its tributaries.

clue.text: Small amount of broth given to prisoner

parts.note: broth is a soup
con, short for convict, is a prisoner

explanation.surface: An inmate is handed a meagre helping of broth.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loan word for a tiny trace or hint of something.

clue.text: In case of emergency, opt for special climbing gear

parts.note: ICE is the phone-contact abbreviation for In Case of Emergency
to opt for is to pick

explanation.surface: Safety advice: in an emergency, choose specialist mountaineering equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers carry these small axes to cut steps and anchor themselves on ice.

clue.text: Playwright who, with time after retiring, could become a children's author!

indicators.note: the clue says the answer plus a letter, turned round, could become another name; so that name reversed, less the letter, gives the answer
retiring means drawing back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A dramatist who, with a bit more time in retirement, might write for children instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: put T before the answer and read it 'retiring', backwards, and you get NESBIT; so NESBIT reversed is TIBSEN, and losing T leaves the dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Leader one hour away from victory

indicators.note: taking letters away from a word removes them

parts.note: a triumph is a victory
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A leading competitor is within an hour of winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a frontrunner but is the card sense: the suit that leads over others.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the trump suit beats all the others, so a trump card is the top, leading card.

clue.text: Each group of journalists has work

parts.note: AP is the Associated Press, a news agency
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Every press agency has its job to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means per item, as in 'five pounds a pop', so each.

clue.text: Northerner's specific motive for being disloyal?

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the definite article, the specific article, is shortened to t'
a reason is a motive

explanation.surface: Someone from the north asks for the precise motive behind a betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern English speech famously clips 'the' to t', so 'the reason' becomes t' reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime of betraying one's country is the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Reindeer quietly scampered round sports ground

parts.note: p, piano, is the music direction for quietly
ran means scampered

indicators.note: turning round sends the word back the other way

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a sports field

explanation.surface: A reindeer silently dashed around the playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Santa's eight reindeer in the poem 'A Visit from St Nicholas', alongside Dasher and Dancer.

clue.text: Officer working steadily, ignoring orders

parts.note: a noncom, short for non-commissioned officer, is an officer such as a sergeant
plying means working steadily at a task

explanation.surface: An officer diligently at work while disregarding instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to obey or conform is the sense, the negative of obeying commands.
